findings.title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder deletes DB row without cancelling in SendGrid when referenceId is absent, and immediate path never removes the DB row
findings.body: When referenceId is null the function deletes the workflowReminder row, but when immediateDelete is true it cancels in SendGrid and returns without deleting the reminder row. Callers (handleCancelBooking, handleNewBooking reschedule path, workflows.delete, step deletion) then rely on the cron to delete it, but the cron only deletes reminders past scheduledDate and cancels cancelled ones within the next hour; reminders with immediate cancel leave stale rows whose referenceId is still a valid batch id, and a subsequent `scheduled` lookup or unique referenceId reuse can misbehave. The asymmetry is confusing and the immediate path is also missing the DB update that the non-immediate path does.

findings.title: Cancelled reminder row is deleted even if SendGrid cancel fails in the batch
findings.body: The loop awaits client.request for each reminder, but the surrounding try/catch wraps the whole loop. If one SendGrid cancel request throws, the loop aborts and all remaining reminders stay cancelled-but-uncancelled in SendGrid and will still be sent, while the already-pushed deletes are awaited. Also the delete promises are created without awaiting inside the loop, so a failed DB delete is only caught by Promise.all and not per reminder. Each reminder should be handled independently so one failure does not block the rest, which is exactly the failure mode this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: SMS cancel deletes reminder row before/regardless of Twilio cancel, and cancelSMS failure leaves SMS sent
findings.body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder now deletes the DB row immediately after twilio.cancelSMS, all within one try. If cancelSMS throws (for example the message already sent or the API fails), the prisma delete is skipped and the row stays, and the caller ignores the failure. Meanwhile it deletes the reminder row even when no referenceId exists, which is correct, but the SMS path is never marked cancelled for later cron processing, unlike the email path. The two managers now use inconsistent cancellation semantics.

findings.title: Errors in deleteScheduledEmailReminder are swallowed, so callers cannot detect failed cancellation
findings.body: The function catches all errors and only logs them. handleCancelBooking and other callers are fire-and-forget (no await), so a SendGrid or DB failure silently leaves the reminder scheduled and it is sent to a cancelled booking, which is the bug this PR claims to fix.

findings.title: Cancellation of workflow reminders is not awaited and no longer checks scheduled state
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach, and the previous guard `reminder.scheduled && reminder.referenceId` was removed. For unscheduled reminders (scheduled=false, referenceId null) the code now runs a DB delete per reminder, and the deletions race with the subsequent Promise.all and with attendee/booking reference deletes. Results of cancellation are not observed before the response is returned.

findings.title: Cancelled flag set for reminders whose cron may already have sent them, and no reset path
findings.body: Setting cancelled=true on reminders is only processed by the cron for those within the next hour. A reminder rescheduled back in (same referenceId, e.g. reschedule creating new reminders) is never un-cancelled, and the cancelled flag is never cleared on creation. Also reminders cancelled but already past scheduledDate are removed by the earlier deleteMany without cancelling in SendGrid, so they may have been sent already with no cancel attempt.

findings.title: Cron cancel reads all cancelled reminders with no batching or limit
findings.body: remindersToCancel is loaded fully and each is cancelled serially via an HTTP request to SendGrid. With many pending cancellations this can exceed the cron timeout and, since the outer try wraps everything, one failure stops the rest, causing the backlog to grow and reproduce the 100-pending-cancellations limit problem described in the PR.

findings.title: Removed PrismaPromise/Prisma type imports while still referenced; import of Prisma as value
findings.body: The import block now imports PrismaPromise and Prisma as runtime values from @prisma/client (they are types) and the type import from the same module was removed; PrismaPromise is still used in the update handler for remindersToDeletePromise. This can break the build under isolatedModules / TS strictness and is inconsistent with the rest of the file.

findings.title: Reindentation of the testAction comment block breaks the commented-out code and the diff is unrelated
findings.body: The large whitespace-only change inside the commented-out testAction block is unrelated to the fix and makes the commented block harder to restore; it also obscures the real changes in review.

findings.title: Sender ID input for SMS actions no longer renders when phone number is not needed
findings.body: The condition changed from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded`, which hides the whole block including the phone number inputs for SMS_ATTENDEE actions. This is an unrelated UI regression not described in the PR; the sender ID field behavior for SMS_ATTENDEE is lost.

findings.title: New cancelled column is nullable Boolean with no default
findings.body: cancelled is Boolean? with no default, so existing and new rows are NULL. The cron filters with `cancelled: true` which is fine, but the field semantics are inconsistent with other flags; a non-null default false would be safer.
